## Task Description
修复 se3 webui running-flow 实时聊天视图在两种场景下「无法持续/正确显示对话记录」的 bug(#193 遗留的另一半,显示发送错误的部分已修复,本次专修「消息不显示」)。包含两个一并修复的症状:

【症状 A — 普通 session:`按1确定` respond 之后实时视图停止追加】
respond(对交互的确认)调用成功后,后续所有对话(agent 自动产出的下一步输出、以及用户之后再发送的消息)都不再出现在实时视图;必须退出再重进 running-flow 视图(触发 `/api/history` 全量快照)才能恢复,且重进后保持正常。该 session 内 `按1确定` 通常只发生一次,故无法稳定确认是否每次发送都触发,但已确认 respond 后必现。需排查并修复 respond(以及对称的 interject)成功后、daemon 推来的 `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` 增量未能到达 `/ws/ui` UI 客户端的问题:重点核查 `server/ws.py` 中「`MSG_HISTORY_DATA` 命中并 resolve 一个 pending REST pull waiter 时抑制对 `/ws/ui` 广播」的逻辑(约 lines 1087-1100),与前端 `app.js` 在 respond 后是否并发触发 REST 拉取所形成的竞态,确保 respond/interject 之后的新记录既能服务 REST waiter、又能正常增量推送给已订阅 ws 的实时视图,无需重进视图即可持续追加。

【症状 B — `--worktree` / discovery session:首条 assistant 回复正文为空,且之后无新消息】
以当前这个 worktree discovery session 为例:聊天框只显示用户初始描述与 assistant 条目的时间戳(`2026/6/14 15:09:44`),assistant 正文完全为空(渲染不出首条回复内容),其后也不再追加任何后续对话。需排查 worktree 会话 history 的读取/解析/增量推送/cursor 推进全链路,定位首条 assistant 正文读不出、且后续不追加的根因:重点核查 sidecar history 文件(`*.jsonl.from-*`)在 `daemon/history.py` 的 `read_flow` / `_iter_history_jsonl` / `_logical_step_id` 及其 cursor 映射中的处理是否完整,以及 worktree 会话的 `project_root` 是否在 respond/interject 与 history 读取链路中被正确保留,确保 worktree/discovery 会话的实时视图能完整、正确地显示首条及后续全部对话正文。

【验收】
1. 普通 session 中 `按1确定`(respond)之后,无需退出重进视图即可持续看到后续全部对话(agent 自动产出 + 用户后续发送的消息)。
2. `--worktree` / discovery session 中,首条 assistant 回复正文正常显示(非空),且后续消息持续实时追加。
3. 修复后运行相关测试(前端实时渲染/合并、`server/ws.py`、`server/state.py`、`daemon/history.py` 覆盖的用例),不得引入回归。

## Changes Made
- modified: src/se3/daemon/client.py
- modified: src/se3/daemon/history.py
- modified: src/se3/server/ws.py
- modified: tests/frontend/live_append_after_respond.test.mjs
- modified: tests/frontend/test_app_pure.mjs
- modified: tests/test_daemon_client.py
- modified: tests/test_daemon_history.py
- modified: tests/test_server_history.py
- modified: tests/test_server_history_live_append_broadcast.py
- modified: tests/test_worktree_history_sidecar.py

## Verification Results
Verification passed: True
Summary: The implementation correctly fixes both halves of the #193-leftover bug. Symptom A (normal session: respond stops live appending) is fixed in server/ws.py by replacing the blanket `if not resolved_pull` broadcast-suppression with `suppress_broadcast = resolved_pull and mode == protocol.HISTORY_MODE_FULL`, so a `mode: append` real-time increment is ALWAYS broadcast to /ws/ui even when it also resolves a pending REST pull waiter — exactly matching the planned [modify_requirement] server::Server Modules declaration. Safety of the always-broadcast append is upheld by the pre-existing frontend `dedupeAppendRecords` already wired into both append consumers in app.js:2666/2693. Symptom B (worktree/discovery session: first assistant body empty + no further records) is fixed in daemon/history.py's full-read path: the previously unconditional consumption of the un-terminated trailing line now branches on JSON parseability — a complete record without trailing newline (terminal/sidecar files) is consumed, while a mid-write truncated tail is left intact (consumed/offset not advanced) so it is re-read once complete. Additionally read_active_flows' final-flush pass now scopes read_flow to each flow's own project_root via a root_by_flow map, and client.py resolves the respond/interject project_root from the history index for worktree/discovery sessions so the .response lands under the correct root — matching the planned [modify_requirement] daemon::Daemon Modules declaration. Sidecar (*.jsonl.from-*) enumeration and _logical_step_id merging are intact. All 254 python tests in the affected suites and the frontend live_append_after_respond + pure tests pass (16 new tests, 0 failures). No unintended changes; the three source files parse cleanly with no leftover removed variables.

## Spec Change Guidance
- [modify_requirement] server: Requirement: Server Modules
  Description: 更新 `ws.py` 对 `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` 广播抑制的描述:抑制 `/ws/ui` 广播仅适用于按需 cache-miss pull 的 `mode: full` 回包;`mode: append` 的实时增量帧即使恰好 resolve 了一个 pending REST pull waiter,也必须继续广播给已订阅的 `/ws/ui` 客户端,以保证 respond/interject 之后实时视图持续追加。
  Rationale: 现行『resolve waiter 即抑制广播』会把同帧承载的实时增量一并吞掉,导致 respond/interject 后实时视图停止追加(症状 A)。需将抑制边界由『是否 resolve waiter』收窄为『是否为 full 回包』。
- [add_scenario] running-flow-console: Requirement: Live-Append Record Deduplication Against Snapshot
  Description: 新增场景:respond/interject 成功后,服务端继续广播 `mode: append` 实时增量(即便该帧也服务了一个 REST pull),前端经 `dedupeAppendRecords` 去重后持续追加且每条记录恰好渲染一次、无需重进视图。
  Rationale: 明确 respond/interject 之后『既服务 REST waiter 又增量推送给 ws』的前后端去重契约,锁定症状 A 的验收行为。
- [modify_requirement] daemon: Requirement: Daemon Modules
  Description: 补充 `history.py` 关于 worktree/discovery 会话读取的描述:`read_active_flows` 的 final-flush 路径必须以正确的 `project_root` 调用 `read_flow`,`_resolve_flow_dir` 必须能定位 worktree 会话的 history 目录,且首条记录(含主文件与 `*.jsonl.from-*` sidecar 归并)的正文必须被完整读出并随 cursor 增量推进,保证 worktree 会话首条及后续对话完整显示。
  Rationale: 现行 final-flush 缺失 `project_root` 及 worktree 会话 root 解析不一致,导致首条 assistant 正文读不出且后续不追加(症状 B)。

## Design Context
### Overview
分两条独立链路修复。链路 A(普通 session 实时流中断):把 `server/ws.py` 中「resolve 了 REST pull waiter 即抑制 `/ws/ui` 广播」的粗粒度逻辑,收窄为「仅抑制按需 cache-miss pull 的 `mode: full` 回包广播」;对 `mode: append` 的实时增量,即使它恰好也 resolve 了某个 waiter,也必须继续广播给已订阅 ws 的实时视图。发起 REST 拉取的客户端经由 `dedupeAppendRecords` 去重不会重复渲染,其余已订阅客户端则能持续收到增量。链路 B(worktree/discovery 首条空 + 后续不追加):在 `daemon/history.py` 的 sidecar 读取链路(`read_flow`/`_iter_history_jsonl`/`_logical_step_id` + cursor 映射)与 `read_active_flows` final-flush、`_resolve_flow_dir` 的 `project_root` 解析上,确保 worktree 会话的 `project_root` 被完整保留并能定位到正确的 history 目录,首条 assistant 正文与后续记录均能被读出并增量推送。

### Components
- **server/ws.py — MSG_HISTORY_DATA 广播分支**: 在 resolve pull waiter 后,按 `mode` 决定是否广播:`mode == full` 且 resolve 了 pull 则抑制(REST 回包负责送达);其余(含所有 `mode == append` 实时增量)始终调用 `_push_history_data` 广播给该 owner 的 `/ws/ui` 客户端。
- **server/state.py — append_history / get_history_snapshot**: 确认 `append` 在 bundle 存在时正确 extend 并返回 `applied=True`、保持 generation 稳定;确保被广播的 append 与 REST 全量回包对同一 bundle 快照一致,不产生 token/generation 漂移。
- **daemon/history.py — sidecar 读取与 cursor/root 解析**: 保证 `_iter_history_jsonl` 同时枚举 `*.jsonl` 与 `*.jsonl.from-*`;`_logical_step_id`/`parse_step_type_from_step_id` 正确归并;`read_flow` 首条记录正文被读出、cursor/`_read_offsets` 正确推进;`read_active_flows` final-flush 传入 `project_root`;`_resolve_flow_dir` 正确定位 worktree 会话目录。
- **daemon/client.py — project_root 在 respond/interject 与 history push 链路保留**: 确保 respond/interject 处理与 `_push_history`/`read_active_flows` 调用链中,worktree 会话的 `project_root` 不丢失(尤其 final-flush 与 `_resolve_interject_root` 路径)。
- **static/app.js — applyHistoryData / 实时追加去重**: 确认 respond/interject 后,服务端放行的 append 帧经 `dedupeAppendRecords` 去重后正确追加渲染,既不重复也不丢失;worktree 首条记录 normalize 后正文非空(若源头已修则仅校验)。

### Architecture Decisions
- **症状 A 的根因修复落在服务端 `ws.py`/`state.py`,而非依赖前端绕过。**
  Rationale: 记录已正确到达服务端缓存(重进视图触发全量快照即恢复证明缓存完整),失败的只是 `/ws/ui` 增量广播这一跳;在广播抑制点按 `mode` 收窄是最小、最精确的修复面,且对所有订阅客户端一致生效。
- **区分 `mode: full`(按需 pull 回包,抑制广播)与 `mode: append`(实时增量,始终广播),而非区分「是否 resolve 了 waiter」。**
  Rationale: 抑制广播的真正目的是避免把 cache-miss pull 的全量帧再广播出去导致全体客户端 progress token 被清空;该目的只针对 `mode: full`。`mode: append` 帧无论是否凑巧 resolve waiter,都承载实时增量,必须送达订阅者。
- **症状 B 在 `daemon/history.py`/`client.py` 内修复 `project_root` 保留与 sidecar 首条解析,前端仅做兜底校验。**
  Rationale: 首条正文为空且 cursor 不前进是读取侧问题:final-flush 路径 `read_flow(flow_id, cursor=cursor)` 缺失 `project_root` 会导致 `_resolve_flow_dir` 在错误的 roots 集合中查找;worktree 会话的 root 解析需统一。源头修好后前端 `normalizeRecord` 无需特例。
- **前端复用既有 `dedupeAppendRecords`/`reconcileLocalEchoes`/`mergeSnapshotWithLiveAppends`,不新增第二套去重路径。**
  Rationale: running-flow-console 规范已要求 append 路径经 `dedupeAppendRecords` 去重;服务端放行 append 后产生的「REST 响应 + ws 广播」重叠正落在该函数的设计职责内,只需补测试确认覆盖 respond/interject 后场景。

## Specs Directory
/data/cre/workspace/se3.0/se3/worktrees/worktree-webui-1-session-bug-bug-20260614-150938-2d556aa7/se3/specs

## Spec Access Protocol (index-first — do NOT read whole specs or the index cache)

Obtain spec context through the read-only `se3 spec` index commands. You MUST
NOT, for the purpose of gathering context, read an entire large spec file with
the Read tool, and you MUST NOT read the index cache file
`se3/cache/spec-index.json` directly — it is an internal, program-maintained
format, not an LLM-facing surface.

- `se3 spec index` — root view: every spec's name, a one-sentence locator, and item count. Start here.
- `se3 spec index <spec> [<group>...]` — drill into one spec's Requirement index (id / title / summary / tags); trailing group-path components open a folded domain group or a `pN` page.
- `se3 spec show <spec>::<requirement>` — the authoritative body of ONE Requirement plus its physical location (file path + 1-based inclusive line range).

**Directed edit of an existing Requirement (no whole-file reads):** to modify a
Requirement that already exists, FIRST run `se3 spec show <spec>::<requirement>`
to obtain its physical location (file path + line range), THEN Read ONLY that
line range and Edit it in place. Never read the whole spec file for a localized
change.

## base Spec Admission Standard

The `base` spec is the ONLY spec injected — in full — into every step of every
session. Its size is therefore a fixed cost paid on every single LLM call, and
neither on-demand loading nor index drill-down can reduce it. Keep it small and
top-level.

`base` MAY carry ONLY content that every session genuinely needs loaded in full:

- Project identity / positioning (what this project is, its primary language /
  framework).
- The global architecture picture (the top-level directory map, how the major
  pieces fit together).
- Cross-cutting conventions that apply project-wide (coding conventions, key
  constraints, workflow conventions).
- A one-line locator index of each module / spec (the name plus a single
  sentence pointing at where its detail lives).

`base` MUST NOT carry module-specific detail. Anything that belongs to one
subsystem — its submodule list, its internal mechanics, its per-step behaviour —
belongs in that module's own spec, reachable on demand via `se3 spec index` /
`se3 spec show`, NOT in `base`. When a write would push `base` over its
configured size limit, the new content MUST be routed into the corresponding
module spec rather than appended to `base`.

## Spec Writing Discipline

Each layer of the spec index is derived mechanically (no LLM) from text that
already exists in the spec at write time. Follow these rules so that derived
text is navigable:

(a) Each Requirement's body SHALL open its first paragraph with a one-sentence,
    summary-level overview. The index truncates that opening paragraph (first
    ~200 chars) into the item's entry summary, so a leading throwaway sentence
    yields a useless summary.
(b) Each spec's `## Purpose` section SHALL open with a one-sentence locator that
    states, in a single line, what the spec is about. The root index view shows
    each spec's name plus this one-sentence locator.
(c) Each spec SHALL declare a `<!-- domain: <layered/path> -->` header marker
    alongside the `<!-- spec-format: v1 -->` marker. The domain path is how the
    root view groups specs when it grows past its size threshold.
(d) Section organisation SHALL keep the number of items under any single `###`
    section moderate; avoid hanging an excessive number of Requirements off one
    section heading. (The renderer paginates over-large groups as a fallback, so
    this is guidance, not a hard checked rule.)

## Spec Split Criteria (cohesion first, size second)

A spec growing past its size warning threshold is a *signal to evaluate*, not an
order to split. Apply cohesion before size:

- If the over-sized spec is multi-topic (its items cluster into groups with
  sparse cross-cluster references), it SHOULD be split into parallel specs.
- If the spec is internally cohesive and merely long, do NOT force a split. Its
  byte size does not pressure the LLM context under the size-bounded index, and
  it should be slimmed gradually via the per-Requirement discipline instead.

Responsibility split:

- Splitting into parallel specs is a semantic-level refactor (it produces a new
  spec name and must update logical addresses, cross-spec refs, the index, and
  domain metadata). It is performed ONLY by `se3 sync`, with the split plan
  confirmed by the user through sync's respond channel.
- `update_spec` MUST NOT create a parallel spec on its own. When it judges that
  a spec should be split, it only records the recommendation in its output and
  leaves the split to `se3 sync`.

## Instructions
1. Use the index-first protocol above to locate the spec(s) and Requirement(s) that need updating — `se3 spec index` to navigate, `se3 spec show` to read a specific Requirement's body and its physical location. Do NOT read whole spec files or the index cache.
2. If Spec Change Guidance is provided above, use it as your primary checklist for updates — execute each declared change intent (add, modify, deprecate) in the corresponding spec files. This is your guided mode.
3. If no Spec Change Guidance is available, determine which specs need updating by analyzing the changes made and verification results. This is the inference mode.
4. Use the Edit tool to directly modify the spec files — for an existing Requirement, do a directed Read+Edit on the physical line range returned by `se3 spec show`, never an integral read of the whole file. Follow existing formatting conventions.
5. Only update specs that genuinely need changes — do not rewrite specs unnecessarily.
6. Follow spec guardrails: do NOT delete existing requirements, only add or modify.
7. If Design Context is provided, use it to understand the architectural rationale behind changes — this helps produce more accurate and well-motivated spec updates.
8. Respect the base Spec Admission Standard above: when adding content would push the `base` spec over its size limit, route that content into the corresponding module spec rather than appending it to `base`.

## New Spec Decision (Mandatory)

Consult the root index view appended below (the same view as `se3 spec index`),
which lists every existing spec with a one-sentence locator, to check for naming
collisions and to decide whether the new content belongs in an existing spec.

Before appending ANY new Requirement to an existing spec, you MUST evaluate the following four criteria. ALL four must pass to append; if ANY fails, create a new spec.

1. **Conceptual Independence** — The new content shares the same conceptual domain as the existing spec. It is about the same subsystem, mechanism, or abstraction level. If the content introduces a fundamentally different concept (e.g., "how to format JSON" into a spec about "error handling patterns"), it fails this test.

2. **Dependency Direction** — The new content does NOT cause existing Requirements in the spec to depend on it. If adding the Requirement would force older Requirements to reference or assume the new behavior (e.g., an existing "Retry Logic" Requirement now needs to know about a new "Circuit Breaker" Requirement), the dependency direction is wrong and a new spec is needed.

3. **Naming Test** — The new Requirement can be naturally named under the existing spec's title. A reader encountering the Requirement name should not be surprised to find it in this spec. If the name feels like it belongs in a different category, it fails this test.

4. **Cross-Scenario Reusability** — The new content is NOT expected to be referenced by multiple unrelated capabilities. If the content is a cross-cutting concern (e.g., "Authentication", "Configuration Format", "Versioning Rules") that multiple specs will need to cite, it should be its own spec to avoid circular references and provide a single source of truth.

**Decision rule:**
- If ALL four criteria pass → **append** the new Requirement to the existing spec.
- If ANY criterion fails → **create a new spec** at `se3/specs/<new_name>/spec.md` with standard structure (Purpose, Requirements, Scenarios).

**Scope of this decision — placement of NEW content only (NOT splitting an existing spec).**
This four-criteria decision governs only where to put the *new* Requirement(s)
this flow introduces: append them to an existing spec, or carve out a brand-new
spec for a genuinely independent subsystem. It does NOT authorize you to relocate
or carve up the *existing* content of an over-sized multi-topic spec. Splitting an
already-existing spec into parallel specs is a semantic-level refactor reserved
EXCLUSIVELY for `se3 sync` (see the Spec Split Criteria above). If, while placing
new content, you observe that the target existing spec is over-sized and
multi-topic and ought to be split, do NOT split it or create the parallel spec
yourself — only record the split recommendation in your `notes` and leave the
actual split to `se3 sync`. The "create a new spec" branch here is for the new
subsystem's own content, never a vehicle for migrating an existing spec's
Requirements into a freshly created parallel spec.

When creating a new spec:
- Choose a concise, kebab-case directory name (e.g., `issue-discovery`, `test-runner`).
- Add `<!-- spec-format: v1 -->` as the first line.
- Immediately after the format marker, add a `<!-- domain: <layered/path> -->` header marker declaring the new spec's domain — a slash-separated classification path (e.g. `engine/steps`, `server/auth`) that places the spec above the spec level so the root index can group it. Choose the domain from where the subsystem lives relative to the existing specs in the root view.
- Open `## Purpose` with a one-sentence locator stating, in a single line, what the spec is about (the root view shows each spec's name plus this locator).
- Include `## Requirements` with at least one `### Requirement: <name>`, and `#### Scenario:` blocks.

When you are done, output a JSON summary:
```json
{
    "specs_updated": [
        {
            "spec_name": "name-of-spec",
            "change_description": "What was changed and why"
        }
    ],
    "new_capabilities": ["capability1", "capability2"],
    "spec_decisions": [
        {
            "requirement_name": "Name of the new requirement",
            "decision": "append|new_spec",
            "target_spec": "spec-name where requirement was placed",
            "reasoning": "Brief justification referencing which criteria passed/failed"
        }
    ],
    "notes": "Any additional notes"
}
```

- `spec_decisions` is REQUIRED whenever you add a new Requirement. If you only modified existing Requirements, return an empty array.
- If no spec updates are needed at all, return empty arrays for both `specs_updated` and `spec_decisions`.


IMPORTANT: You MUST respond in en-US in the update_spec step. Preserve all technical symbols verbatim in their original form — do NOT translate code identifiers, function/class names, command names, API names, file paths, or literal config keys/values. This content is written into a spec file: the configured spec language (en-US) is authoritative. Write all prose and every SHALL/MUST requirement statement in en-US.

## se3 Runtime Environment

You are running inside an se3-managed project. The lists below tell which se3 commands are safe to call proactively, and which are not.

### Safe to call proactively (read-only)

**View past session history** — trigger on 上一个 session / 上次 / 之前的 session / 上次跑到哪了 / 历史记录 / 前几次的对话 / 刚才那次, or similar references to prior runs.

Overview & navigation (preferred first):
- `se3 history list` — list recent flow runs
- `se3 history show <flow_id>` — show structured details of one run
- `se3 history archived` — list archived engine state snapshots

Free-form content search (fallback):
- `se3/history/<flow_id>/<step>.jsonl` — full conversation per step
- `se3/state/archive/engine_*.json` — archived engine state snapshots

**Recommended workflow:** 先用 `se3 history list` 找到目标 `<flow_id>`，再用 `se3 history show <flow_id>` 看结构概貌；若需按关键词搜索，则 `grep -r '关键词' se3/history/<flow_id>/`。

**Consult related issue context** — trigger when the task references an issue, or the user mentions an issue ID.

Overview & navigation (preferred first):
- `se3 issue list` — list issues
- `se3 issue show <id>` — show issue details

Free-form content search (fallback):
- `se3/issues/open/*.yaml`, `se3/issues/closed/*.yaml`

**Recommended workflow:** 先用 `se3 issue list` 看清单；若需按关键词搜索 issue 内容，则 `grep -r '关键词' se3/issues/`。

### Do NOT call proactively

以下 se3 命令存在但**不在你应主动调用的范围**，除非用户在当前会话中**明确要求**：

- `se3 history restore` — rolls back flow state
- `se3 issue create` / `se3 issue reset` — write operations; do not create issues on your own
- `se3 salvage` — auto-commits, creates issues, archives sessions
- `se3 merge` / `se3 merge respond` — mutates git merge state
- `se3 sync` / `se3 sync respond` — modifies spec files
- `se3 init` — only for initializing brand-new projects

# running-flow-console::Live-Append Record Deduplication Against Snapshot
# location: /data/cre/workspace/se3.0/se3/worktrees/worktree-webui-1-session-bug-bug-20260614-150938-2d556aa7/se3/specs/running-flow-console/spec.md:443-535

### Requirement: Live-Append Record Deduplication Against Snapshot

A running flow's conversation (and the history view) is built from two sources
that can deliver the **same** records: the `GET /api/history/{flow_id}` snapshot
fetched by `loadFlowConversation` / `openHistorySession`, and the incremental
`history_data` appends pushed over the `/ws/ui` channel and merged by
`applyHistoryData`. On the server, `ws.py` handles `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` by first
writing the cache (`state.append_history`) and then broadcasting the batch to UI
(`_push_history_data`). When a snapshot fetch lands in the window **after** the
cache write but **before** the WS broadcast arrives, the snapshot already
contains that batch; the subsequently-arriving `history_data` append for the
**same** batch would then be `concat`-ed in a second time. The result is a batch
of records (non-interactive `user` / `system` prompt chips, `step_completed`
report cards, etc.) rendered twice during live streaming, which vanishes on a
manual reload because the reload re-fetches the clean, non-duplicated server
cache. The view MUST suppress this duplication on the **append** path so each
record is held — and rendered — exactly once, without changing the daemon push
logic, the server `append_history` / `_push_history_data` cache-then-broadcast
order, or the WS protocol. This is a **pure-frontend** fix: the server cache
itself is never duplicated, so `mergeSnapshotWithLiveAppends` is left unchanged.

`mergeSnapshotWithLiveAppends` already dedups the *opposite* race — appends that
arrive **during** the fetch `await` — but it cannot cover appends that arrive
**after** the fetch has already resolved into state. The two symmetric races are
therefore each owned by one pure function, both keyed on the **same** record
identity function `recordKey`:

1. **`dedupeAppendRecords(existing, incoming)`** — a new DOM-free, side-effect-free
   exported pure function (same export-block pattern as
   `mergeSnapshotWithLiveAppends` / `historyListEmptyState`). It builds a
   `Set(existing.map(recordKey))` and returns only those `incoming` records whose
   `recordKey` is not already present in `existing`: an empty array when every
   incoming record is already held, an array equivalent to `incoming` when all are
   new, and the new-only subset otherwise. Because `partial` / `stream_progress`
   segmented records' `recordKey` naturally varies as their content accumulates,
   later fragments of the same streaming record are NOT falsely deduped.
2. **Both append consumers filtered** — `applyHistoryData`'s append branch MUST
   run `incoming` through `dedupeAppendRecords` against the *current* held array
   before merging, for **both** the running-flow view (`state.flowConversationRecords`)
   and the history view (`state.historyRecords`). When the filtered result is
   empty, that consumer MUST short-circuit: it makes no state change and triggers
   no render, preserving the existing incremental semantics (no spurious
   re-render). When the result is a non-empty subset, only the genuinely new
   records are `concat`-ed, so the `st.count` incremental-cursor render path
   (`renderConversation` / `renderHistoryRecords`) and the downstream stick
   judgement / `reconcileLocalEchoes` calls keep working unchanged.

The `mode: full` (non-append) snapshot-replacement path is NOT affected by this
dedup — it replaces the held array wholesale and is left exactly as-is.

#### Scenario: Same batch in snapshot and live append is held once
- **GIVEN** a snapshot fetch for a running flow resolves in the window after the
  server wrote a `history_data` batch to its cache but before the matching WS
  `history_data` append has been delivered, so the snapshot already contains that
  batch
- **WHEN** the WS `history_data` append for the **same** batch later arrives and
  `applyHistoryData` runs its append branch
- **THEN** `dedupeAppendRecords` filters out every record whose `recordKey` is
  already present in the held array, so no record is `concat`-ed a second time
- **AND** the conversation / history record array contains no duplicate
  `recordKey`, and the batch is rendered exactly once

#### Scenario: Append of all-already-present records makes no change
- **GIVEN** an incremental `history_data` append whose records are all already
  held in `state.flowConversationRecords` (or `state.historyRecords`)
- **WHEN** `applyHistoryData` filters the append through `dedupeAppendRecords`
- **THEN** the filtered result is empty and that consumer short-circuits — no
  state mutation and no re-render — preserving the incremental-render semantics

#### Scenario: Append with a mix of seen and new records merges only the new ones
- **GIVEN** an incremental append whose records partly overlap the held array by
  `recordKey` and partly introduce new `recordKey`s
- **WHEN** `applyHistoryData` filters the append through `dedupeAppendRecords`
- **THEN** only the records with previously-unseen `recordKey`s are `concat`-ed
- **AND** the `st.count` incremental cursor advances by exactly the number of new
  records, so `renderConversation` / `renderHistoryRecords` render only the
  genuinely new tail

the I/O is done via the injected `registry_load` / `registry_persist` callbacks), concentrating persistence at a single write-through point rather than scattering it across the four registration call sites, ensuring no registration is missed; `all_project_roots()` is the sole source of this merged view, both producing `MachineStatus.project_roots` via the `_merge_project_roots` delegate and serving as the `project_roots_provider` for the history index's `build_index` (see `daemon.py` / `history.py`), so that even with zero live processes, or after a daemon restart, neither the history list nor the New Task dropdown is empty anymore; per-flow snapshot polling (`get_snapshot`) still uses only the `_project_roots` active set, avoiding polling all historical roots every tick. To keep this merged view cheap on the hot path, `all_project_roots()` always merges the **active base** (`_project_roots ∪ registry_load`) immediately, but the expensive **disk historical enumeration** (`enumerate_historical_project_roots`, which walks the whole `se3/history` tree) is throttled behind a monotonic-clock TTL cache (`HISTORICAL_ROOTS_TTL`, currently `60s`) keyed/invalidated by a fingerprint of the active base, collapsing the per-tick full traversal to at most one walk per TTL window; the cache must be invalidated correctly without busting on the routine re-add of already-known active roots, and `add_project_root` proactively invalidates it so a newly registered root's history becomes visible promptly. This field is reported via `STATUS_UPDATE` to drive the Project dropdown of the web New Task form, covering the "active set is empty but historical projects are still usable" scenario after a daemon restart; when enumerating pending-response calls under `se3/calls/`, items that already have a same-named response file (`.response` / `.response.json`) are skipped, to avoid a historically already-answered call being misreported as pending; besides this sibling-response determination, `_enumerate_calls` / `_snapshot_for_root` must also decide whether a pending call is still valid based on the flow's current progress: when a call's owning `context.step_id` is no longer the flow's current step (or that step has already been processed as `COMPLETED` / `REVISION`), the call must be removed from that flow's `pending_calls` even if no `.response` sibling file was written — because interactive calls answered at the CLI terminal (`call` / `cli_confirm` / `discovery_confirm`) are usually consumed directly by the run loop without writing a sibling file, otherwise a stale "awaiting reply" chip would never clear for the whole run; a call still sitting at the current unanswered step stays pending. In addition, for the same `(flow_id, step_id)` only the latest unanswered call is kept (`_dedup_calls_by_step`): discovery's multiple clarification rounds reuse the same `step_id`, writing a new call file each round, and once an old call is superseded by a new round it becomes a stale leftover and must be removed from that flow's `pending_calls` to prevent "awaiting reply" chips from accumulating; a call whose key cannot be located (missing `flow_id` or `step_id`) does not participate in deduplication and is kept as is. Each call file's `kind` field (`call` / `interjection` / `retry_decision` / `cli_confirm`, treated as `call` when absent) is parsed and, together with the `prompt` / `context` / `options` display metadata, enriched into a `PendingCall` and reported via `STATUS_UPDATE`, so the web console can render the various pending interactions differently by `kind`. In addition to calls, the aggregator reads each project's `se3/issues/` YAML files (via `_collect_issues`) into a list of `IssueSnapshot` entries carried on `MachineStatus.issues`, so the webui issue-management panel can list / filter / view issues without a second round-trip; each `IssueSnapshot` carries the webui-relevant fields (`id`, `project_root`, `description`, `status`, `tags`, `source`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, plus the optional `title` / `priority` / `type` which are omitted when unset), defaulting a missing `source` to `system` for legacy files, and unreadable issue files are skipped so a corrupt issue never breaks the snapshot. **Worktree issue de-duplication.** A `se3 run --worktree` flow clones the project's `se3/issues/` into its sandbox, so while the run is live both the main project root and the worktree-copy root would otherwise be aggregated and every issue would be counted twice. The aggregator MUST therefore skip issue collection for any project root that is a worktree copy (`is_worktree_copy_root`, see `supervisor.py`): during a worktree run only the main project's issues are authoritative, and the worktree copy's `se3/issues/` are ignored, so the webui issue list and counts are not doubled. (This is the same `se3/worktrees/` attribution that keeps the worktree directory out of the project list.) **Promoted worktree terminal state.** Because the merge-back promotes a completed worktree flow's terminal `engine.json` into the main project's `se3/state/archive/engine_<flow_id>.json` (see the `se3-workflows` spec), the aggregator/history layer reports that promoted snapshot as a `completed` flow exactly like an ordinary archived run, with no worktree special-case

The CLI counterpart `PersistenceManager.extract_history_summary` (see the se3-commands spec) applies the identical three-tier priority, differing only in that it clips its own result to 100 characters. Reads incrementally by per-flow per-step jsonl file cursors, so an active session's conversation records can be reported incrementally without re-sending the whole jsonl each round. While reading, it also parses the authoritative step_type from each per-step jsonl filename (convention `NN_<step_type>_<hash>(_Gk)`) and injects it at the envelope layer, so each reported record looks like `{step_id, step_type, message}`: the raw `message` pushed by the daemon itself does not contain step_type, and after injection the frontend no longer has to guess from the filename, while the `message` content is left untouched to maintain backward compatibility and raw visibility. The parsing is done by the pure function `parse_step_type_from_step_id(stem)` — after stripping the leading `NN_` sequence number, the trailing `_G\d+` group suffix, and the trailing hexadecimal hash segment, it takes the remaining middle segment (which may itself contain underscores, e.g. `version_analyze`) as the step_type, softly validated against the built-in `_KNOWN_STEP_TYPES`; when the naming convention is followed but the type is unregistered it still returns the parsed middle segment (self-describing, drift-tolerant), while an old name with no sequence number and no hash (e.g. `commit_summary`) falls back to the original stem, never raising. The "active" determination of `read_active_flows` must cover **in-progress** flows (including `PAUSED` waiting for user input and the `--resume` continuation state), and must not prematurely drop a flow merely because it is not at the RUNNING terminal value, otherwise the web would freeze during a run and only catch up all at once after archiving; the incremental cursor must advance correctly on each round's read — newly appearing per-step jsonl files and appended lines of the same file must all be taken in, achieving **no loss, no duplication, no truncation of subsequent reads** (a record once read is never re-read, and an unread tail continues next round). To keep the daemon's per-fast-tick push loop (`client.py::_push_loop` → `_push_history`, which calls `build_index` every ~1s tick) from re-walking the whole `se3/history` tree every second — a second event-loop-starvation source distinct from, but of the same class as, the aggregator's `enumerate_historical_project_roots` walk already throttled by `HISTORICAL_ROOTS_TTL` — `build_index` caches its result behind a monotonic-clock TTL (`BUILD_INDEX_TTL`, currently `3s`): within the window it returns the cached `SessionMeta` list and only the uncached `_build_index_fresh()` performs the full directory walk + JSON parse, collapsing the repeated identical per-tick rebuilds into at most one walk per window. `invalidate_index_cache()` drops the cache so the next `build_index` rebuilds from disk; it is called on every real disk change (the push loop invalidates when `_history_changed()` fires), right after a flow is spawned, and before a forced index re-push (all three call sites live in `client.py`), so a newly spawned or just-changed flow becomes visible promptly rather than waiting out the TTL. Because the cached index may carry **stale `active` flags** for up to the TTL window, `read_active_flows` no longer trusts `meta.active` directly: it re-checks each candidate's live status via `_is_still_active`, a lightweight single-`engine.json` `stat` + small JSON parse (dramatically cheaper than the full rebuild it replaces) that confirms the on-disk `engine.json` still describes *this* `flow_id` (guarding against a different flow having since become the active `engine.json` flow, which would otherwise keep the stale meta in the active set and miss the new flow) and that its status is still an active one — so liveness is preserved (any real `engine.json` / jsonl change invalidates and rebuilds fresh, and the per-flow re-check catches within-window status flips) while the TTL collapses the redundant full walks that were starving the event loop. It also exports the helper `enumerate_historical_project_roots() -> list[str]`: it traverses `se3/history/<flow_id>/_meta.json` and `se3/state/archive/engine_*.json`, extracts each record's `project_root` field, and deduplicates and sorts them, for `aggregator.py` to merge into `MachineStatus.project_roots` when rebuilding the snapshot; when fed the union "active roots ∪ persistent registry roots" (rather than the active set only), it supplements each root in the union with its on-disk history roots, robustly skipping non-directory / artifact-less roots without raising. The two WARNING points that report an unreadable / corrupt archive or `_meta.json` file (`history: skipping unreadable meta file ...` and the sibling archive-file warning) are **per-file deduplicated** (`_warn_once_unreadable`): the first encounter of a given path logs at WARNING, and every subsequent encounter of the same path is demoted to DEBUG, so a small set of permanently corrupt meta files can no longer flood `daemon.log` (the observed failure produced a ~210MB / ~1.26M-line log from four corrupt `_meta.json` re-warned every tick). This dedup is a defence-in-depth backstop independent of, and complementary to, the TTL throttling of the enumeration in `aggregator.py` (which already drives the warning frequency down at the source); the corrupt files themselves are left in place and continue to be ignored. The `project_roots_provider` of the history index construction (`build_index`) is injected by the daemon as `aggregator.all_project_roots` (the ordered union of active roots ∪ registry roots ∪ the aforementioned on-disk history roots), replacing the previous approach of directly reading the bare active set `aggregator.project_roots` — the latter is empty when "this machine currently has no se3 run process", which was exactly the root cause of the history list previously always coming up empty (`No history sessions reported.`); after switching to `all_project_roots`, the history index is still non-empty with no live processes, or even after a daemon restart. To eliminate a second-order regression that 57b1609 (8.11.2)'s `BUILD_INDEX_TTL` cache addressed only partially — where the per-tick push loop still rebuilt the index roughly once per second (an active flow writing to disk every second fires `invalidate_index_cache()` via `client.py`, defeating the 3s TTL), and each `_build_index_fresh()` rebuild called `_extract_history_summary` on every history-only directory lacking a `_meta.json`, which read the entire first jsonl via `read_text()` just to take its first line (observed: 161 such directories, ~115MB of first jsonl including a single 30MB stale discovery log, sustaining ~100MB/s logical reads with a single core pinned at ~92% CPU by CPython's UTF-8 decode at ~104 MB/s; ZFS arcstats confirmed the reads were ~99.4% ARC-cache hits so the cost was single-core CPU burn and degraded daemon responsiveness rather than physical-array wear) — the whole-file reads in `history.py` are replaced by bounded reads via three changes:
22	  1. `_extract_history_summary` streams only the first line (`open()` + `readline()`) instead of `read_text()`, so recovering a title never reads the whole file; its three-tier output (the `prompt_markers.extract_user_content` user literal, then the `Task description:` block, then the raw first line) is unchanged, so the daemon→web title and its CLI counterpart (`PersistenceManager.extract_history_summary`, see the se3-commands spec) stay aligned.
23	  2. `DaemonHistoryReader` gains a process-internal per-directory meta cache (`self._history_meta_cache: Dict[str, Tuple[signature, SessionMeta]]`) keyed by a cheap directory content signature (the set of jsonl filenames + the latest mtime + total size, computed by reusing the existing `iterdir`/`stat` traversal); `_meta_from_history` returns the cached `SessionMeta` on a signature hit and only parses + back-fills on a miss, so a `_build_index_fresh` rebuild re-parses only the directories whose signature actually changed (an active flow's per-second write changes only its own directory's signature, while the other ~161 static directories all hit the cache). This is a process-internal optimization only: it does NOT write to disk and does NOT back-fill `_meta.json` into project directories (the daemon never writes into project directories on their behalf). It layers beneath the existing `BUILD_INDEX_TTL` cache: the TTL cache suppresses an entire rebuild on a no-change tick, while the per-directory signature cache suppresses re-parsing the unchanged directories during a rebuild that a real change did trigger.
24	  3. `read_flow` reads active flows incrementally by **byte offset** instead of `read_text().splitlines()` re-reading the whole jsonl every push and slicing by a line-number cursor. A process-internal `self._read_offsets: Dict[str, Tuple[consumed_lines, byte_offset, mtime, size]]` keyed by absolute jsonl path lets a push seek to the recorded offset and read only the appended bytes when the caller's line cursor matches the recorded consumed-line count and the file size is ≥ the recorded offset; otherwise (first read / cursor rewind / file truncated-and-replaced) it falls back to a from-scratch full read and rebuilds the offset, with the UTF-8 byte-boundary seek handled correctly. Only complete `\n`-terminated lines are consumed; a trailing partial line is left for the next round — a strictly safer compatibility improvement over the prior full-read path, which under a write race would treat a half-written line as bad JSON, skip it, and advance the cursor, dropping a record. The external `FlowRead` line-number cursor semantics and the pushed `records` content are preserved item-for-item, so server / webui keep using the `{jsonl-filename: line-count}` cursor unchanged; the offset table is reader-internal optimization state that never enters the wire protocol, so after a daemon restart it cold-starts and the first round degrades to a single full read, with correctness independent of it.
25	  The remaining file-read point `_read_json` was reviewed and left unchanged because it only reads small JSON files; these are the three file-read points in `history.py` (the first-jsonl title extractor, the active-flow incremental reader, and `_read_json`).

27	  **Worktree merge-back sidecar files.** When a `se3 run --worktree` flow merges back, each worktree per-step history file is written into the main session directory not as a plain `*.jsonl` but as a collision **sidecar** named `<base>.jsonl.from-<branch>` (e.g. `01_discovery_ab12.jsonl.from-worktree__b`), because the logical-step file may already exist in the main session. A reader that enumerates only `glob("*.jsonl")` never matches these sidecars, so every record after the first is dropped and the frontend renders empty content as "(no readable content)". The history reader MUST therefore enumerate **both** the primary `*.jsonl` files **and** their `*.jsonl.from-<branch>` sidecars, and merge them under one **logical step id**: the pure helper `parse_step_type_from_step_id` / the step-id reduction strips the `.jsonl` extension together with any trailing `.from-<branch>` sidecar suffix (and a possible trailing hash) before parsing `step_type`, so a step's primary file and each of its sidecars resolve to the same logical step and stream together. Because the incremental read cursor is keyed by **absolute file path**, each primary and each sidecar advances independently, so a worktree merge-back that only appends sidecar records is still picked up with no loss, no duplication, and no truncation — both the running-flow live stream and the post-merge completed history of a `--worktree` session display in full, exactly like an ordinary in-place session
28	- `protocol.py` — the single source of truth for the daemon↔server WebSocket protocol: `PROTOCOL_VERSION` (currently `"2"`), `DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT` (the central server's default port `8080`, referenced by both the `--port` default of `se3-server` and the daemon client's URL port completion), `MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES` (the shared daemon↔server WebSocket single-frame size cap, currently `256 * 1024 * 1024` = 256 MiB; both ends import this one constant so the inbound size limit cannot drift between them — the daemon passes it as `max_size` to `websockets.connect` and the server passes it as `ws_max_size` to `uvicorn.run`, lifting the libraries' much smaller defaults (`websockets`' 1 MiB and `uvicorn`'s 16 MiB) that would otherwise silently drop an oversized `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` frame and surface as a `GET /api/history/{flow_id}` 504; a bounded large value is used rather than `None` so a pathologically large frame still has a memory ceiling), the message-type constants (`MSG_HELLO` / `MSG_WELCOME` / `MSG_STATUS_UPDATE` / `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW` / `MSG_RESPOND_CALL` / `MSG_CALL_NOTIFICATION` / `MSG_PING` / `MSG_PONG`, plus the history-related `MSG_HISTORY_INDEX` (daemon→server historical session index) / `MSG_HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST` (server→daemon, requesting the daemon to rebuild and immediately re-push its historical session index, registered into `SERVER_TO_DAEMON` / `ALL_MESSAGE_TYPES`) / `MSG_HISTORY_REQUEST` (server→daemon, on-demand pull of a historical session's records) / `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` (daemon→server historical-data response, supporting full / append modes and a cursor), plus `MSG_INTERJECT_FLOW` (server→daemon, dispatching one mid-flight interjection typed in the web console to a running flow)) and the `make_*` message constructors (including `make_history_index` / `make_history_index_request` / `make_history_request` / `make_history_data` / `make_interject_flow`; `make_spawn_flow` adds a `discover` field to pass through the "start from discovery" flag, **and an optional `resume_flow_id` field** — when non-empty it is included in the payload and instructs the daemon to *resume* the named flow (`se3 run --resume --flow-id <id>`) rather than start a fresh one, with `task_description` ignored in that case; when empty it is omitted from the wire so a fresh-spawn payload is unchanged and stays backward compatible. `make_spawn_flow` further accepts an **optional `from_issue_id` field**: when non-empty it is included in the payload and instructs the daemon to start the flow from the named issue (`se3 run --from-issue <id>`), in which case the request's `task_description` is ignored in favor of the issue's content and the issue lifecycle is driven by the CLI; it MAY be carried together with the `discover` field (start-from-discovery on an issue), and when empty it is omitted from the wire so existing fresh-spawn payloads are byte-for-byte unchanged and no `PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump is required). The module also defines the **issue write-command message pair** for the webui issue-management surface: `MSG_ISSUE_COMMAND` (server→daemon, registered in `SERVER_TO_DAEMON`) carries an `operation` of `create` / `edit` / `close` / `reopen`, a required `project_root`, operation-specific fields (`issue_id`, `description`, `title`, `priority`, `type`, `tags`, `reason`) and an optional `request_id`; `MSG_ISSUE_RESULT` (daemon→server, registered in `DAEMON_TO_SERVER`) echoes the `request_id` with `ok=true` or `ok=false`+`error` (and the affected `issue_id`) so the server can correlate the acknowledgment. Their constructors are `make_issue_command(operation, project_root, *, issue_id, description, title, priority, type, tags, reason, request_id)` (which omits unset optional fields, and where for `edit` a `None` field means "leave unchanged" while an empty string means "clear") and `make_issue_result(request_id, *, ok, error, issue_id)`. This module also centrally defines the `kind` constants `CALL_KIND_*` (`CALL_KIND_CALL` / `CALL_KIND_INTERJECTION` / `CALL_KIND_RETRY_DECISION` / `CALL_KIND_CLI_CONFIRM`) and the `CALL_KINDS` set for the running-flow human-interaction call files, so that the `kind` value of call files under `se3/calls/` does not drift among the engine, the daemon, and the server. It is imported by both the daemon and the `se3.server` package, ensuring the protocol schema does not drift. A peer encountering an unknown `type` should ignore it, to guarantee that mixed old/new version connections do not crash. For the multi-tenant control plane, `make_hello(machine_id, hostname, se3_version, key="")` carries an **optional** `key` field — the daemon credential the server resolves to an owner (`key → owner_id`) to bind the reporting machine to a trust domain; the field is omitted from the wire when `key` is empty, so a keyless daemon and an older single-tenant server stay wire-compatible (no `PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump), and the key is a secret that MUST NEVER be logged. `make_welcome(server_version, accepted=True, reason="")` carries the `accepted` flag and a (key-free) `reason` string so the server can reject an unauthenticated/invalid-key HELLO with `WELCOME(accepted=false)`

input.old_string: Only complete `\n`-terminated lines are consumed; a trailing partial line is left for the next round — a strictly safer compatibility improvement over the prior full-read path, which under a write race would treat a half-written line as bad JSON, skip it, and advance the cursor, dropping a record.
input.new_string: The handling of an **un-terminated trailing line** (a final line not closed by `\n`) MUST branch on JSON parseability rather than always being deferred: a trailing line that already parses as a complete JSON record — the normal shape of a terminal-written file and of every `*.jsonl.from-<branch>` merge-back sidecar, whose final (and, for a single-record file, only) record is frequently flushed without a closing newline — is **consumed** and advances the offset, while a tail that does not yet parse (a genuine mid-write truncated line) is **left intact** (consumed-line count and byte offset are NOT advanced) so it is re-read once the writer completes it. This is the root cause of the worktree/discovery symptom-B "first assistant body empty, then nothing further": the prior "only consume `\n`-terminated lines" rule deferred the complete-but-unterminated first/only record indefinitely, so the worktree session's first assistant record read as empty and the cursor never advanced past it. The parseability branch keeps the prior write-race safety (a half-written line is still never skipped-and-dropped) while no longer starving a complete record of its trailing newline.

# server::Server Modules
# location: /data/cre/workspace/se3.0/se3/worktrees/worktree-webui-1-session-bug-bug-20260614-150938-2d556aa7/se3/specs/server/spec.md:12-37

### Requirement: Server Modules

`src/se3/server/` is the standalone package for the central-server backend plus its bundled web frontend; it isolates the heavy web dependencies via `pyproject.toml` optional-dependencies (`se3[server]`) and is launched through the separate console_scripts entry point `se3-server` — not built as a subcommand of the core `se3`. New server submodules must be registered in this spec.

- `app.py` — the FastAPI application entry point: `create_app` assembles the routes, `run` / `main` start it via `uvicorn` (the `uvicorn.run` call is given `ws_max_size=protocol.MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES` so the server's inbound frame limit is lifted off uvicorn's 16 MiB default to the shared protocol cap — this is the limit that was silently dropping oversized daemon→server `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` frames and surfacing as a `GET /api/history/{flow_id}` 504) and parse `--host` / `--port` / `--version` (`--version` is only a completeness supplement to the argparse help text; the real interception happens in `src/se3/server/__init__.py:main` before FastAPI / uvicorn are imported, with output format `se3-server version {__version__}` aligned with the core `se3 version`); it provides a REST API (machine / flow queries, remotely publishing new tasks, answering pending call/interjection) and mounts `static/` at `/`; `create_app` wires the multi-tenant auth/identity layer **fail-closed**: it constructs the `Store` (sqlite, from `server.db_path`), the `SessionStore`, the `LoginRateLimiter`, the `IdentityService`, and the `ProviderChain` (via `build_provider_chain`, raising `AuthNotConfigured` and refusing to start when no usable provider is configured), and every `/api/*` data route carries `Depends(require_owner)` so an unauthenticated request is rejected with 401; the resolved `OwnerIdentity` is mapped to an owner scope (`_scope_for`) and threaded into the `ServerState` query methods so all machine / flow / history reads are owner-filtered, and `POST /api/flows` / `respond` / `interject` first verify the target machine / flow belongs to the current owner (a foreign target reads as 404), closing the prior identity-unaware remote-command-dispatch hole; `POST /api/flows` additionally accepts an optional `from_issue_id` parameter (composable with the existing `discover` parameter): when supplied, the server resolves the issue owner-scoped (reusing `ServerState.get_issue_by_id(..., owner=...)`, so an issue on a machine/project outside the caller's owner scope — or an unknown id — reads as 404) to obtain the authoritative target machine/project, then threads `from_issue_id` through `make_spawn_flow` to the owning daemon so the spawned flow is started from that issue (the request's `task_description` being ignored in that case); the auth surface adds `POST /api/auth/login` (username+password → session cookie), `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` (the current `OwnerIdentity`), and `POST /api/auth/breakglass` (consume a one-time break-glass token → the single stable break-glass admin owner, lazily created via `_ensure_breakglass_admin`); the owner self-service surface adds `POST /api/daemon-keys` (mint a daemon key bound to the current owner, returning the plaintext once), `GET /api/daemon-keys` (list the owner's key metadata), and `DELETE /api/daemon-keys/{key_id}` (revoke); and the admin-gated user-management surface — every route independently enforcing `Depends(require_owner)` + an `is_admin` check (a non-admin caller is rejected 403, before any existence check so the surface leaks nothing) via a shared `create_app`-local `_require_admin` guard, never relying on the frontend hiding the entry — comprises `POST /api/users` (create / invite a local user), `GET /api/users` (list manageable owners as a strict field whitelist — `owner_id` / `display_name` / `is_admin` / `created_at` / identity `provider` / a `can_reset_password` flag — never returning password or daemon-key hashes or any other sensitive field, with the break-glass owner filtered out server-side by reverse-resolving its reserved `(BREAKGLASS_PROVIDER, …)` binding), `DELETE /api/users/{owner_id}` (delete a user, cascading the cleanup of its bindings / credentials / daemon keys via `store.delete_owner` under `ON DELETE CASCADE` foreign keys), `POST /api/users/{owner_id}/password` (reset password — only for `local`-provider owners, reusing `crypto.hash_password` + `store.set_password` with the plaintext hashed off the event loop and never logged; # running-flow-console::Live-Append Record Deduplication Against Snapshot
# location: /data/cre/workspace/se3.0/se3/worktrees/worktree-webui-1-session-bug-bug-20260614-150938-2d556aa7/se3/specs/running-flow-console/spec.md:443-535

### Requirement: Live-Append Record Deduplication Against Snapshot

A running flow's conversation (and the history view) is built from two sources
that can deliver the **same** records: the `GET /api/history/{flow_id}` snapshot
fetched by `loadFlowConversation` / `openHistorySession`, and the incremental
`history_data` appends pushed over the `/ws/ui` channel and merged by
`applyHistoryData`. On the server, `ws.py` handles `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` by first
writing the cache (`state.append_history`) and then broadcasting the batch to UI
(`_push_history_data`). When a snapshot fetch lands in the window **after** the
cache write but **before** the WS broadcast arrives, the snapshot already
contains that batch; the subsequently-arriving `history_data` append for the
**same** batch would then be `concat`-ed in a second time. The result is a batch
of records (non-interactive `user` / `system` prompt chips, `step_completed`
report cards, etc.) rendered twice during live streaming, which vanishes on a
manual reload because the reload re-fetches the clean, non-duplicated server
cache. The view MUST suppress this duplication on the **append** path so each
record is held — and rendered — exactly once, without changing the daemon push
logic, the server `append_history` / `_push_history_data` cache-then-broadcast
order, or the WS protocol. This is a **pure-frontend** fix: the server cache
itself is never duplicated, so `mergeSnapshotWithLiveAppends` is left unchanged.

`mergeSnapshotWithLiveAppends` already dedups the *opposite* race — appends that
arrive **during** the fetch `await` — but it cannot cover appends that arrive
**after** the fetch has already resolved into state. The two symmetric races are
therefore each owned by one pure function, both keyed on the **same** record
identity function `recordKey`:

1. **`dedupeAppendRecords(existing, incoming)`** — a new DOM-free, side-effect-free
   exported pure function (same export-block pattern as
   `mergeSnapshotWithLiveAppends` / `historyListEmptyState`). It builds a
   `Set(existing.map(recordKey))` and returns only those `incoming` records whose
   `recordKey` is not already present in `existing`: an empty array when every
   incoming record is already held, an array equivalent to `incoming` when all are
   new, and the new-only subset otherwise. Because `partial` / `stream_progress`
   segmented records' `recordKey` naturally varies as their content accumulates,
   later fragments of the same streaming record are NOT falsely deduped.
2. **Both append consumers filtered** — `applyHistoryData`'s append branch MUST
   run `incoming` through `dedupeAppendRecords` against the *current* held array
   before merging, for **both** the running-flow view (`state.flowConversationRecords`)
   and the history view (`state.historyRecords`). When the filtered result is
   empty, that consumer MUST short-circuit: it makes no state change and triggers
   no render, preserving the existing incremental semantics (no spurious
   re-render). When the result is a non-empty subset, only the genuinely new
   records are `concat`-ed, so the `st.count` incremental-cursor render path
   (`renderConversation` / `renderHistoryRecords`) and the downstream stick
   judgement / `reconcileLocalEchoes` calls keep working unchanged.

The `mode: full` (non-append) snapshot-replacement path is NOT affected by this
dedup — it replaces the held array wholesale and is left exactly as-is.

#### Scenario: Same batch in snapshot and live append is held once
- **GIVEN** a snapshot fetch for a running flow resolves in the window after the
  server wrote a `history_data` batch to its cache but before the matching WS
  `history_data` append has been delivered, so the snapshot already contains that
  batch
- **WHEN** the WS `history_data` append for the **same** batch later arrives and
  `applyHistoryData` runs its append branch
- **THEN** `dedupeAppendRecords` filters out every record whose `recordKey` is
  already present in the held array, so no record is `concat`-ed a second time
- **AND** the conversation / history record array contains no duplicate
  `recordKey`, and the batch is rendered exactly once

#### Scenario: Append of all-already-present records makes no change
- **GIVEN** an incremental `history_data` append whose records are all already
  held in `state.flowConversationRecords` (or `state.historyRecords`)
- **WHEN** `applyHistoryData` filters the append through `dedupeAppendRecords`
- **THEN** the filtered result is empty and that consumer short-circuits — no
  state mutation and no re-render — preserving the incremental-render semantics

#### Scenario: Append with a mix of seen and new records merges only the new ones
- **GIVEN** an incremental append whose records partly overlap the held array by
  `recordKey` and partly introduce new `recordKey`s
- **WHEN** `applyHistoryData` filters the append through `dedupeAppendRecords`
- **THEN** only the records with previously-unseen `recordKey`s are `concat`-ed
- **AND** the `st.count` incremental cursor advances by exactly the number of new
  records, so `renderConversation` / `renderHistoryRecords` render only the
  genuinely new tail

# server Specification

## Purpose

The standalone central-server backend (`se3-server`) plus bundled web frontend, its multi-tenant identity/auth/persistence model, and the owner-scoped REST/WebSocket surfaces.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Server Modules

`src/se3/server/` is the standalone package for the central-server backend plus its bundled web frontend; it isolates the heavy web dependencies via `pyproject.toml` optional-dependencies (`se3[server]`) and is launched through the separate console_scripts entry point `se3-server` — not built as a subcommand of the core `se3`. New server submodules must be registered in this spec.

the resolved `OwnerIdentity` is mapped to an owner scope (`_scope_for`) and threaded into the `ServerState` query methods so all machine / flow / history reads are owner-filtered, and `POST /api/flows` / `respond` / `interject` first verify the target machine / flow belongs to the current owner (a foreign target reads as 404), closing the prior identity-unaware remote-command-dispatch hole; `POST /api/flows` additionally accepts an optional `from_issue_id` parameter (composable with the existing `discover` parameter): when supplied, the server resolves the issue owner-scoped (reusing `ServerState.get_issue_by_id(..., owner=...)`, so an issue on a machine/project outside the caller's owner scope — or an unknown id — reads as 404) to obtain the authoritative target machine/project, then threads `from_issue_id` through `make_spawn_flow` to the owning daemon so the spawned flow is started from that issue (the request's `task_description` being ignored in that case); the auth surface adds `POST /api/auth/login` (username+password → session cookie), `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` (the current `OwnerIdentity`), and `POST /api/auth/breakglass` (consume a one-time break-glass token → the single stable break-glass admin owner, lazily created via `_ensure_breakglass_admin`); the owner self-service surface adds `POST /api/daemon-keys` (mint a daemon key bound to the current owner, returning the plaintext once), `GET /api/daemon-keys` (list the owner's key metadata), and `DELETE /api/daemon-keys/{key_id}` (revoke); and the admin-gated user-management surface — every route independently enforcing `Depends(require_owner)` + an `is_admin` check (a non-admin caller is rejected 403, before any existence check so the surface leaks nothing) via a shared `create_app`-local `_require_admin` guard, never relying on the frontend hiding the entry — comprises `POST /api/users` (create / invite a local user), `GET /api/users` (list manageable owners as a strict field whitelist — `owner_id` / `display_name` / `is_admin` / `created_at` / identity `provider` / a `can_reset_password` flag — never returning password or daemon-key hashes or any other sensitive field, with the break-glass owner filtered out server-side by reverse-resolving its reserved `(BREAKGLASS_PROVIDER, …)` binding), `DELETE /api/users/{owner_id}` (delete a user, cascading the cleanup of its bindings / credentials / daemon keys via `store.delete_owner` under `ON DELETE CASCADE` foreign keys), `POST /api/users/{owner_id}/password` (reset password — only for `local`-provider owners, reusing `crypto.hash_password` + `store.set_password` with the plaintext hashed off the event loop and never logged;
